Description: Follow-up for recurrent tachyarrhythmia after electrical cardioversion, respiratory symptoms, and leg edema.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: The patient returns after a second electrical cardioversion performed yesterday for an irregular, rapid heartbeat. He reports that sinus rhythm was restored. He previously experienced cough with hemoptysis, treated with antibiotics; the bloody sputum has resolved, although he continues to describe chest rattling and difficulty clearing secretions. He reports fatigue, sleepiness, and shortness of breath which he associates with metoprolol and other cardiac medications. His feet and ankles had become markedly swollen. He used borrowed diuretic tablets with some improvement because he had not obtained a prescription. He awaits further cardiology evaluation and asks whether a pacemaker may be needed.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY: Recurrent cardiac arrhythmia requiring two cardioversions. Recent cough with hemoptysis and dependent edema.
MEDICATIONS: Recent cardiac medications include metoprolol and Coumadin. The patient has used diuretics obtained from another individual. Inhalers and cough preparations were discussed.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION: Chest auscultation was performed. The examination details are not fully stated in the transcript.
IMPRESSION AND PLAN: Status post successful cardioversion with reported normal rhythm. After discussion with the supervising clinician, the patient was instructed to discontinue metoprolol and Coumadin and was directed to obtain prompt cardiology follow-up. He was advised to attend the emergency department for recurrent palpitations, significant dyspnea, or other symptoms suggesting recurrent arrhythmia. Repeat echocardiography was planned. The possibility of ablation and pacemaker placement was explained as a contingency if the rhythm problem returns or cannot be controlled, rather than a current scheduled procedure. The patient's edema and inappropriate use of another person's diuretic were discussed, with consideration of a prescribed diuretic.
